'''Klaus Fredenhagen''' (born 1 December 1947) is a German [[theoretical physics|theoretical physicist]] who works on the mathematical foundations of [[quantum field theory]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://unith.desy.de/people/allmembers/fredenha/|title=Klaus Fredenhagen personal homepage|access-date=March 28, 2021|website=Hamburg University|archive-date=April 20, 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210420153424/https://unith.desy.de/people/allmembers/fredenha/|url-status=dead}}</ref>

== Biography ==
Klaus Fredenhagen was born on 1 December 1947 in [[Celle]], a German city in [[Lower Saxony]]. He graduated in 1976<ref>The doctoral thesis is {{cite thesis|last=Fredenhagen|first=Klaus|date=1976|title=Die Quantenelektrodynamik mit einem Freiheitsgrad für das Photonfeld|lang=de|url=https://katalogplus.sub.uni-hamburg.de/vufind/Record/039673154|place=Hamburg|archive-date=2021-04-19|access-date=2021-03-29|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210419210353/https://katalogplus.sub.uni-hamburg.de/vufind/Record/039673154|url-status=dead}}</ref> from the [[University of Hamburg]] under the supervision of Gert Roepstorff and [[Rudolf Haag]].<ref>{{MathGenealogy|id=66111|title=Klaus Fredenhagen}}.</ref> In 1985 he became a [[privatdozent]] and in 1990 a [[full professor]] at the second theory institute of the Hamburg University.<ref>He was the successor of Rudolf Haag's chair, who retired in 1987. See e.g. the historical overview {{cite web|url=https://www1.physik.uni-hamburg.de/en/th2/ueber-das-institut.html|title=About the Theoretical Physics Institute II|access-date=March 29, 2021|website=Hamburg University|archive-date=April 18, 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210418080153/https://www1.physik.uni-hamburg.de/en/th2/ueber-das-institut.html|url-status=dead}}</ref> Since 2013 he has been a [[professor emeritus]] and has continued to be active in research.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.hpk.uni-hamburg.de/resolve/id/cph_person_00002964|title=Fredenhagen, Klaus|access-date=March 29, 2021|website=Hamburg University|language=de}}</ref>

== Scientific career ==
His research interests are [[algebraic quantum field theory]] and [[quantum field theory in curved spacetime]]. In 1981 he proved the existence of [[antiparticle]]s in massive quantum field theories without using the [[CPT symmetry|CPT-invariance]].<ref>{{cite journal|last = Borchers|first = Hans-Jürgen|title = The CPT theorem in two-dimensional theories of local observables|journal = Communications in Mathematical Physics|volume = 143|pages = 315–332|year = 1992|issue = 2|doi = 10.1007/BF02099011|bibcode = 1992CMaPh.143..315B|s2cid = 120842877|url = https://projecteuclid.org/euclid.cmp/1104248958}}</ref> In 1990 he and Rudolf Haag made important contributions to the understanding of the [[Hawking radiation]] of [[black hole]]s on a rigorous mathematical footing.<ref>{{Cite book|first = Bernard S.|last = Kay|date = 2006|article = Quantum Field Theory in Curved Spacetime|title = Encyclopedia of Mathematical Physics|pages = 202–212|publisher = Academic Press|isbn = 978-0-12-512666-3|doi = 10.1016/B0-12-512666-2/00018-3|arxiv = gr-qc/0601008|s2cid = 16258638}}</ref> In 1994, together with [[Sergio Doplicher]] and John E. Roberts, he investigated the mathematical foundations of [[quantum gravity]] in terms
of the quantum structure of spacetime at the [[Planck scale]].<ref>{{Cite book|last1=Bahns|first1=Dorothea|last2=Doplicher|first2=Sergio|last3=Morsella|first3=Gerardo|last4=Piacitelli|first4=Gherardo|date=2015|editor1-last=Brunetti|editor1-first=Romeo|editor2-last=Dappiaggi|editor2-first=Claudio|editor3-last=Fredenhagen|editor3-first=Klaus|editor4-last=Yngvason|editor4-first=Jakob|chapter=Quantum Spacetime and Algebraic Quantum Field Theory|title=Advances in algebraic quantum field theory|pages=289–330|publisher=Springer, Cham|isbn=978-3-319-21353-8|doi=10.1007/978-3-319-21353-8_7|arxiv=1501.03298|s2cid=118886773}}</ref> In 1996, together with Romeo Brunetti, he started working on the generalization of the Epstein-[[Vladimir Jurko Glaser|Glaser]] renormalization procedure of interacting quantum field theories in curved spacetime using techniques from the [[microlocal analysis]].<ref>{{cite book|editor1-last=Brunetti|editor1-first=Romeo|editor2-last=Dappiaggi|editor2-first=Claudio|editor3-last=Fredenhagen|editor3-first=Klaus|editor4-last=Yngvason|editor4-first=Jakob|last1 = Khavkine|first1 = Igor|last2=Moretti|first2=Valter|date = 2015|chapter = Algebraic QFT in Curved Spacetime and Quasifree Hadamard States: An Introduction|title = Advances in Algebraic Quantum Field Theory|series = Mathematical Physics Studies|pages = 191–251|publisher = Springer International Publishing|isbn = 978-3-319-21352-1|doi = 10.1007/978-3-319-21353-8|bibcode=2015aaqf.book.....B }}</ref> He is currently working, together with [[Detlev Buchholz]], on a new [[C*-algebra|C*-algebraic]] approach to interacting quantum field theories.<ref>{{cite journal|last1=Buchholz|first1=Detlev|last2=Fredenhagen|first2=Klaus|title=A C*-algebraic approach to interacting quantum field theories|journal=Communications in Mathematical Physics|volume=377|pages=947–969|year=2020|issue=2|doi=10.1007/s00220-020-03700-9|arxiv=1902.06062|bibcode=2020CMaPh.377..947B|s2cid=92987721}}</ref>

== Honors and awards ==
In 1987 Klaus Fredenhagen was awarded the physics prize of the [[Göttingen Academy of Sciences]]<ref>{{cite web|url=https://adw-goe.de/en/awards/categories/preise-fuer-biologie-fuer-chemie-und-fuer-physik/#c4501|language = de|title=Physics prize winners|website=Göttingen Academy of Sciences|access-date=March 30, 2021}}</ref> and in 1997 he was Leibniz Professor<ref>The Leibniz Professorship is one of the highest honor awarded by the University of Leipzig and it is granted every semester since 1994. See {{cite web|url=https://www.ral.uni-leipzig.de/en/support/leibniz-programme/leibniz-professorship/|title=Leibniz Professorship|access-date=March 29, 2021|website=Leipzig University}}</ref> at the [[University of Leipzig]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.ral.uni-leipzig.de/unterstuetzung/leibniz-programm/leibniz-alumni/|title=Leibniz Alumni|access-date=March 29, 2021|website=Leipzig University}}</ref> In December 2017 the workshop ''Quantum Physics meets Mathematics'' was held in honor of his 70th birthday at the University of Hamburg.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.lqp2.org/node/1424|title=Quantum Physics meets Mathematics - a workshop on the occasion of Klaus Fredenhagen's 70th birthday|access-date=March 28, 2021|website=Local Quantum Physics Crossroads}}</ref>
